learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.

Has aptitude to apply acquired knowledge on the following topics of Differential and Integral Calculus: Real and complex numbers; limits and continuity of functions of one and several variables; differential and integral calculus of one and several variables; sequences and series; numerical solution of nonlinear equations, interpolation and numerical integration.
Solves mathematical problems that may arise in Engineering.
Knows how to use numerical methods and mathematical software in solving some mathematical problems.
Has proficiency in handling mathematical language; in particular, symbolic and formal language.
Knows the reflective use of symbolic and numerical calculation tools.
Possesses skills characteristic of scientific-mathematical thinking, which allow asking and answering mathematical questions correctly and rigorously.

syllabus_topics: Real functions of a real variable
teaching_methods: Participatory problem-solving classes in small groups

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (practical tests and academic assignments)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as (Fundamental exam score) x 0.70 + (Advanced exam score OR continuous assessment score) x P. A minimum score above 5.5 points in the fundamental exam is required to consider other scores. P is 0 if the cut-off score is not met, and 0.30 if it is exceeded. To pass the course, a score higher than 5.5 in the fundamental exam and a final grade greater than or equal to 5 points out of 10 possible are required. Students who take the advanced exam waive any continuous assessment grade.
